utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good everyone, everybody. And to you especially, Madam Greffier. Could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. I notice the absence amongst the Defence teams of Mr. Bourgon and Mr. Haynes. The Prosecution, I see Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Vanderpuye. All right. The witness is already present. Ladies and gentlemen, we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis for the first session. Judge Stole will be with us after the first break. Second thing I wanted to tell you is the following: There is a possibility to move tomorrow's and Thursday's sitting from the afternoon to the morning. Of course, given the short notice, we want to make sure that this does not disrupt, particularly you, Mr. Zivanovic, any needs you may have in respect to the witnesses that we will have these two days. What's your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It will be very -- absolutely inconvenient for us to shift the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Both of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Both of them. So you prefer to keep them in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So they will remain in the afternoon as scheduled. Mr. Acimovic, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are proceeding with your testimony, which we started yesterday. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to remind you that yesterday we left it off with my question to which you answered that in your work, you had used the TC 10 piece of equipment which is the telephone switchboard, and that in the course of your work, for a while you worked on establishing wire connections with the battalion. Now I would like to continue along the same lines and ask you to tell me what other pieces of equipment did you use and what other jobs did you have in addition to before or after working on TC 10 and establishing wire lines with the battalion.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on I was again transferred to the military switchboard which was a larger, and I also with worked on TC 10 at the IKM, and also on an RUP 12 piece of equipment at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What is an RUP 12? Can you explain what kind of equipment this is, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a radio relay device, which can have an encrypted device for encrypting and it is only used when the wire connections are down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since you -- since we heard that there were two other radio rely devices, RRU-1, and RRU-800, did you work on these pieces of equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you worked on the switchboard, as you've described for us, how long was your shift during one day? Did you work in shifts and how long was one shift?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, my shift would be 12 plus hours, depending on the number of signalsmen in the brigade. There were times when we had eight hour shifts, so it was not really the same all the time. It all depended on the number of signalsmen that were in the battalion at any given time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were at the forward command post, how long were your shifts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the IKM, our shifts would last for four days and there were two of us signalsmen in that shift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, I was noticing on page 3 at line 17, in the witness's response to the question concerning the signalsmen in the brigade, at that line he indicates signalsmen in the battalion in the same sentence and I was wondering if we could clarify that reference or if it's just an error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye is absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just correct this. When you said that it all depended on the number of signalsmen, what unit did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant signalsmen in the brigade, and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: While being on duty at the IKM, did you have some sort of records that you had to keep? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the IKM, there was a logbook that the signalsmen used to keep and the duty officers also had a logbook that they had to keep.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So we are talking about two different documents, one was used by the signalsmen to enter their notes and the other was used by the duty officers? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were two books, one for us signalsmen and the other for the officers at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were those logbooks always there at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signalsmen's logbook was at the IKM and the duty officer's logbook would be taken to the brigade, which means that it wasn't, the latter wasn't, at the IKM all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell me what you, as a signalsman, when you were on duty at the IKM, what did you enter into your logbook, the logbook kept by the signalsmen? Can you just briefly describe for us what was it that went into that logbook?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would enter everything that we would hear from the battalions, the events in their respective sectors, whether they noticed any movements by the enemy, whether a shell fell anywhere. Whatever they informed us about, we would take note of that and we would also record the time when we heard the piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in July 1995, there was a military operation taking place around the Srebrenica? Do you remember any such event?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether one part of your unit, to be more precise, the Zvornik Brigade, participated in that operation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date when this operation was taking place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact date when people were sent off to Srebrenica, I can't remember that date, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember, or can you tell us, rather, whether you were assigned to go with the group that was dispatched to the operation at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the day when the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. I know when they entered Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During that period of time, from the moment when the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica to a few days after that, what did you do? Were you in the brigade? Were you off duty? What were you doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the brigade working on the switchboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe for us what you were doing at the switchboard? What did your job at the switchboard entail?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work at the switchboard entails establishing connections from the battalion to the brigade and vice versa, establishing connections between anybody calling and anybody in the building, be it the duty operations officer or somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you ever put people through to the brigade commander? Were you in charge of establishing connection between any callers and the person who was in command of the brigade at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was Dragan Obrenovic who was standing in for the brigade commander, and all the calls for commander Vinko Pandurevic were transferred to Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And during those few days, was he regularly at the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely, because our office was on the top floor, the switchboard was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Zivanovic, who are we referring to? Regularly -- who was regularly at the brigade? Vinko Pandurevic or Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just clarify. When you were talking about the person standing in for the commander, who did you have in mind? And who did you put people through? Who did you have in mind when you said that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant Dragan Obrenovic because he was standing in for Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that your office, i.e. the switchboard, was on the third floor. Tell me where were the offices occupied by Mr. Dragan Obrenovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Obrenovic's office was one floor below.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were in charge of -- I withdraw the question. Do you remember who was the duty operations officer at the brigade around that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Working at the switchboard, do you remember any conversations that might have taken place, or topics that prevailed in any of the conversations taking place at the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was on duty at the switchboard at the time, once the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica, the main topic at the switchboard were -- was the movement of the group from Srebrenica towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of group are we talking about? What kind of information did you have about that group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our information, there were several groups in the column. They were armed. Our task or our goal, rather, was to find out what kind of weapons did the groups have, and if possible, to establish what their aim was, where they were headed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When did the first piece of information about that group reach you and how long did the information keep coming in?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first piece of information started arriving immediately upon the moment when the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica, maybe a few hours after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information about possible fighting involving that group? Did you hear about any fighting between that group, on the one side, and the army of Republika Srpska, on the other side?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first there was no fighting at all, and the only task was to monitor their movement. Only a few days later, there was panic in the town of Zvornik because there were no more troops in the brigade, they had all been sent to Srebrenica, Zepa and the separation lines, so the -- our battalion had to be mobilised in order to put up resistance against that column should they have headed towards the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you said our battalion, and this is missing in the translation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: R Battalion. What is the R Battalion? What kind of battalion is that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The R Battalion comprised elderly people who were no longer militarily fit. It also comprised people who had work obligation during the war, as well as people with limited capabilities, people of ill health and similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell me whether you personally, at the time, leave the brigade, leave the brigade command and its perimeter, and if you did, why did you leave it? What kind of task or mission did you get?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm going to object to this question on the grounds that it is vague, there is no reference and with respect to the time that counsel is referring to, either to an event, to a date, or anything of that nature. It's very unclear on the record specifically what days this witness is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then go ahead. Otherwise it's a perfectly legitimate question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me this, please: In the few days following the entry of the VRS to Srebrenica, since you couldn't recall the exact date, but in those few days, did you leave the brigade command perimeter, and if so, what was your task?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did leave it. In the morning, a signalsman, work mate of mine, came, he told me to get ready because we were to go to secure a spot where the communication between the brigade and Memici was interrupted. We took a truck that our unit had been issued with. When we came to the spot where the wires were disrupted, I could see the trail where the column had passed. It was about three metres in width, and the grass and the brush there was basically crushed, there were so many of them. I also saw a car that had been overturned and set on fire. After we fixed that, we returned to the brigade command, whereupon I learned that the vehicle I saw was an ambulance moving from Memici towards the brigade and it had some wounded on board.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember how many days after Srebrenica fell was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think three or five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I won't insist, if you cannot recall it. In the course of the few days after Srebrenica had fallen, and, say, in the course of the next week, within the perimeter of the Zvornik Brigade command, did you see any captured Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please describe what you saw.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was returning from the restaurant. In the hall way of the building I saw a group. I approached to see what was going on. I saw that a military policeman was leading a prisoner who had camouflage uniform on his upper body. On his lower body he had civilian pants. His arm was covered in blood because he had been wounded. He was taken to the outpatient clinic. He was assisted there and they returned some ten minutes later. I followed them to see what was going on. He was taken out in the street and put on board the first bus that came that way. It was then that I saw that some buses were moving towards Bijeljina. There were several. I didn't count them. I asked what it was all about and was told that these were people that had been captured in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 3.00 and 4.00 p.m. I was just leaving after lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether that took place on the same day, when you were sent into the field concerning Memici or did that take place on a different day? Can you give us an estimate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that it was on the same day. We left around 10.00 a.m. to re-establish communication lines, and I saw this around 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Once the VRS entered Srebrenica and in the course of the subsequent week, did you perform any duty shifts at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you relate that to the event when you saw the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how you went to IKM? What means -- by what means, if any?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communications company had been issued with a postal truck, a TAM, with five seats. We were taken to the IKM on board that truck regularly, unless there was an officer accompanying us, in which case we would go by a passenger car and we would all return the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about that day? Did you use the truck or a car? Was any officer with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there on the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Once you arrived there, who did you see there? Who was at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I arrived at the IKM, the only person I saw there was the duty signalsman. There were no officers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During that day, did any officers arrive to be on duty during the time you were there? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No officers arrived during my duty shift. During the shift, however, Commander Vinko Pandurevic came by once, accompanied by two policemen. He asked me whether there was anything new, whether anyone reported anything. He stayed there about 20 minutes and then left the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Save for your commander, did any other officers come during your entire shift? First of all, tell us how long did you stay at the IKM on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed three to four days up there, I believe. I was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that usually there were two signalsmen on duty. Were there any other signalsmen with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember anyone. I said that it depended on the situation. Shifts changed depending on the situation, at the switchboard, work station and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where the IKM was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The IKM was in Kitovnice, at Jerkica hill. There was a weekend cottage. It had one room where the switchboard was and a stove. It also had two smaller rooms with beds in them and a narrow passage in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify, how many rooms were there? I'm not sure whether it was recorded correctly.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two separate rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In total?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did those shifts take place in both rooms? Perhaps you can explain to us how you made use of them during your shifts.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first room, there was a table with a TC 10 device and another RUP 12. There was a side table as well that we used for coffee. In the other room there were two beds. That's where the officers on duty would take their rest. At the beginning, when we started doing shifts there, we also used the beds but some officers objected and we were forced to bring a container, in which we could rest when off duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During your shift, do you remember whether some unusual things took place, something that would otherwise stand out compared to other regular duty days?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my duty at the IKM, two trenches were opened. I'm trying to say that a gap, a space, was made for the column to be able to move on towards Tuzla during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay at the IKM, was there any combat? Could you see or hear anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the IKM, one could not see any combat but one could hear it. You could hear shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a lot of firing, more than usual, or would that be regular, much as the rest of the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. At this point I'm going to object. I think that my friend is leading the witness and he has been for some time but I think at a certain point he should just put the questions directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you talked about the two trenches being opened for the column to pass through, which day of your shift was that, since you spent several days there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was after one or two days. The only thing I know is that when the column was passing through, a soldier was captured and taken over to the Muslim side. I also heard that they asked for some rifles to return that soldier alive. The exchange took place the next day, and indeed he was returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have a few additional questions. While you were in the brigade, not at the IKM, in the brigade, between the day when Srebrenica fell and the day you left for the IKM, were you ever asked to go and stand guard next to some prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of any of your fellow soldiers being asked to perform that duty?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Ostojic, you had requested 15 minutes for cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, yes, thank you, we have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic, you had requested one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but I believe my cross-examination will last shorter than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, please, and could you kindly introduce yourself to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I wanted to introduce myself for the record. My name is Jelena Nikolic. I appear on behalf of Mr. Drago Nikolic in this case. Although I know you since we met here in The Hague last Sunday.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions to clarify some of your answers during today's testimony. Today you said that after Srebrenica had fallen, you spent several days on duty at the Standard where the command of the brigade was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You had open communication with the battalions during that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you sending telegrams to battalions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you sending encrypted or coded telegrams to the battalions in the course of those few days?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We who worked at the switchboard never sent coded telegrams. We only sent written -- I'm trying to say that we would receive written documents and we would read them out, since it was a voice communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You also testified that you were on duty at the IKM as well.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the course of the war, or as of the moment when the IKM was established in Kitovnice, how many times did you go there for your duty shifts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How often? Well, I don't know. Once the IKM was established, I was the first one to go there, and I kept going there until it was closed. Therefore, in the course of that one and a half year, I was there numerous times.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know who of the officers was on duty while you were up there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many. There was Jokic, Major Jokic. There was Trbic, Mr. Drago Nikolic, Sreten Milosevic, Jovo --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you ever on duty together with Major Mihajlo Galic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the whole period of my shifts at the IKM, I was with him the least, perhaps once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did that perhaps take place in the days following the fall of Srebrenica, while you were up at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was on duty in the wake of the fall of Srebrenica, none of the officers were up there at the IKM, as I've already stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In course of your testimony, you described the devices that you had at the forward command post. This is my question: Did you have a device enabling you to listen in on the enemy and their communications?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were unable to intercept enemy communications at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did there exist an interception station or listening station for the purposes of the brigade, for the purposes of the army, that you were able to use?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There existed a listening station called premier, which was at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the name of the location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, can you repeat the name of the location, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gucevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you have contacts with Premier at Gucevo while you were at the forward command post and did you exchange messages with them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the IKM. We did have contacts with Premier in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: However, if a message from Premier was sent to the Zvornik Brigade, it could be received only at the command post and not at the Kitovnice forward command post, if my understanding is correct.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was on duty, Premier never placed a call to Kitovnice. Rather, he directly approached the brigade command and conveyed information there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your testimony today, you said that signalsmen had their own duty logbook and officers had their own. I believe you did not have occasion to review an officer's logbook but nevertheless you would be familiar with the outward appearance of the book?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had our own logbook, and the officers had their own. We were not privy to their logbooks, and we were not interested in reading them. They were supposed to write the same things we did, because they were reading our logbook and it depended entirely on them as to what information contained in our logbook would end up in theirs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can the witness be shown Exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit 377, page -- or rather pages 130 and 131 in the B/C/S and pages 24 and 25 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, while we are waiting for the document to appear on our screens, let me explain to you that this is a logbook of the duty operations officer of the brigade and I'm interested in his entries. You may not have seen the document before but when I show it to you, I'll ask you to explain to me precisely what we have been discussing right now, Premier, and the messages received from that quarter. Page 130.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move it up where it starts with 1503?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, do you see the entry for -- or rather the entry which says, "1503, Semso"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Semso preparing an action, Premier sends this message.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you read on?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Premier asks for --" I can't read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 131 now? Can you please look at the entry that we have at the top of the page, starting with the word --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Premier entered --" rather, we have "premier" and then it says "entered, has entered, has come in."

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: "And cleared of mines"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Has entered and cleared of mines." Or probably "has cleared the area between dugouts or something, cleared of mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that all the three entries we've looked at originated with the Premier or rather he was the one who sent them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he sent these messages, Premier sent these messages.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It says here that an attack is being prepared and that the enemy has broken through our positions, through the houses or piles or something?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the column to be able to pass through.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can we have P935? Page 8 in the B/C/S and 6 in English. Mr. Acimovic, this is a logbook kept by the duty officer at the IKM. The entry is for the 14th of July, as was the case with the other logbook we were looking at. Mr. Acimovic, please focus on the entry for the 14th of July 1995, the second paragraph starting with, "The enemy forces."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't make out what it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why? Why is it? Because it is too small? What's your problem? Or because you can't read the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't read the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To me it's big enough but maybe if we could try to zoom in a little bit, magnify it a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can read this out for the witness, unless my learned friends object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We have the original book if you would prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. Show him the original book but to me this is clear enough. It's only that I don't understand the --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Or she can read it. I have no position on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. There is no position. There is no objection, Madam Nikolic, if you wish to read the entry. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I will read this out for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: "The enemy forces through the communications devices very active and conducting preparations for an attack on our forces. According to what has been announced, they cleared several areas of mines that had been laid there for the purposes of the attack." Did you understand what I've just read out, Mr. Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have a question for you. As a signalsman, present at the IKM, were you able to listen in on the communications of the enemy and were you able to conclude if the enemy was very active on the communications lines and were you able to convey such information at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The enemy communication lines could not be listened into at the IKM. That much I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And one was not able to know if the enemy was active, was busy communicating and preparing for an attack?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's objectionable and that is calling for speculation on the part of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't want the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think it's an unnecessary question because if the witness confirms that there was no way they could intercept, why put the second question? But anyway, it's up to you to withdraw this question and move to the next or if you wish to put the same question, you need to rephrase it in a way which makes it intelligible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will withdraw the question. You're right. The witness has fully answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have several questions left for you, Mr. Acimovic. From your experience as a signalsman, can you tell us what the title of your Kitovnice IKM was within the communications system?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name for the IKM was Palma 2. That was how we introduced ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was your basic task at the IKM to maintain communications with seven battalions of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We checked our communications arm, meaning the IKM communications with the battalions on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: One more question: Did you know the family by the name of Jerkic at Kitovnice?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were our next-door neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did the signalsmen have any dealings with the family?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They would visit us quite often, bring us milk and food that they had prepared for us. We were on very good terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Whoever was on duty at the IKM had to be acquainted with the Jerkic family; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were on good terms with everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci, Madam. Mr. Lazarevic? You had requested 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we did, but we are not going to cross-examine this witness, his evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Madam Fauveau, s'il vous plait.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci, Madam. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We have no questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Sarapa, equally so?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We never announced that we would cross-examine. However now we do have some questions which would probably take no more than five minutes probably, so we would kindly ask to you allow us to put some questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Sarapa, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Acimovic, I'm Djordje Sarapa I'm appearing for Vinko Pandurevic in this case.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: A few very short questions for you. Can you tell me whether you know where Cajici Brdo is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Was that at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether the commander, and I'm referring to Mr. Vinko Pandurevic, at the time when you were up there and when you were talking about the events that you witnessed at the IKM, whether he commanded from the observation post?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no telephone at the observation post. There was a line which means when an officer arrived at the observation post, the signalsman who was off at the time had to go to the observation post, he had to establish a telephone line with Palma 2, so I did not see Mr. Pandurevic ever being at the observation post or at least he never asked any of us to come and accompany him and at the time I was on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you know whether, from the observation post or from the IKM, you could observe the positions of the 4th Infantry Battalion at the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally went to the observation post only once. There was no need for me to go there. Our duty was to be at the switchboard, save for those occasions when an officer would ask us to accompany them to the observation post. This would be the only time when we went. I did not watch out for the lines of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. I would like to ask -- thank the Chamber for allowing me to put the questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sarapa. Mr. Vanderpuye, you had asked for an hour and a half. How long do you expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I expect it will be somewhat shorter than that, Mr. President, hopefully for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead and start, and if you can cut it even further, it will be better. So in the meantime make sure staff, registrar, that the next witness is properly groomed, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it would be all right with the Court I would prefer we take a break first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I was going to suggest it but I held back not knowing whether I would have everyone agreeing to it. We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Acimovic. My name is Kweku Vanderpuye. I'm an attorney with the Prosecution. I'm going to ask you a few questions in relation to your direct testimony. You testified on your direct examination that you had been dispatched to the area of Memici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you testified that you were dispatched at some point to go and repair certain lines. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was dispatched to repair the lines with the Memici Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you indicated that you left for that purpose, the command of the brigade, at around 10.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you were dispatched to that area you also indicated that you saw a vehicle that you later learned was an ambulance that had been set on fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the time that you observed the ambulance, was it on fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was just smoke. The vehicle was not on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So when you saw it, it was still smoking? I'm sorry, I didn't receive a translation of the answer. When you saw the vehicle, was it still smoking?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was just some smoke, not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did that occur in the vicinity of Planinci village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the vicinity of Crni Vrh, where we were dispatched to in order to repair the line. That's where the line had been disrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that in the area, the same area, where you saw the ambulance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same area, the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have in e-court, please, 65 ter 377? And we need the 02935619 complete version and it's page 139 in both the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, what I want to show you an entry from the duty officer's notebook for the 15th of July and if I could, could we make our way down the page? Okay. Right there where it says it appears to be "nestao." Could you read that? Have you had a chance to read that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this appeared with the wounded Velibor Pekic, Milos Tesic, Mladen Stevic, around 6.45, between Crni Vrh and Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that the incident you're referring to or the circumstances that you were referring to when you say that you saw an ambulance in that area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no other vehicles. There was no other ambulance when we were dispatched to the field around 10.00, 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But what I mean is that that is the area in which you saw the ambulance that's indicated in this entry, on the road between Crni Vrh and Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crni Vrh, Orahovac, yes, and we re-established the line below Crni Vrh in the direction of Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. After you repaired the line, you went back to the brigade command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you've indicated that you're not sure if it was on that day that you saw some prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I wasn't sure. It is possible that I saw them on that day between 1500 and 1600 hours. On that day, I was dispatched around 10.00, so I'm not sure whether I saw the prisoners the day before or on that same day. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. But in any event, you were dispatched to this area where you saw the ambulance from the brigade command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't know that the ambulance would be there where the line was disrupted. We had been informed that the line had been disrupted and I went to provide security for the place because we knew that the column was moving in that direction and we had to stand there with rifles until the moment the line was repaired, and when we arrived, we saw that the cables had been broken right in the place where the column had moved through and it is in that place where we also saw the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. All right. You testified earlier that you went to the IKM at some point after you saw this ambulance; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN ACIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that I went to the IKM -- actually, I saw the prisoner, I repaired the line, and then on the following day, I went to the IKM, but I wouldn't be able to give you the exact date of any of these events. I can't tell you whether my sighting of the prisoner coincided with the other thing or not or maybe it was one day before or one day after, I'm not sure. Which means that on the following day I went to the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is the following day after you saw the ambulance or after you saw the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually I don't think the witness has answered the question. He's indicated he's done three things and he doesn't recall specifically what order they were done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the answer. He didn't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. And if he doesn't recall, how is he going to give you an answer to your last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He doesn't recall which order he did the three things and I'm asking him specifically in relation to two of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if he can be more precise. Mr. Acimovic, can you be more precise in your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said the following: I saw both these things and then I went to the IKM, which means I saw the prisoner, I saw the ambulance, I repaired the line, and then I went to the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that, Mr. Acimovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, we don't have any questions, further questions, for you, neither from parties nor from the Bench, which means that your testimony finishes here. And you will be escorted out of the courtroom by our staff. On behalf of the Trial Chamber I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony and I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no exhibits for tendering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the exhibits that have been shown to the witness are already in evidence, so we don't have any other documents to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And you, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same. Same position, all right. Thank you. That concludes the testimony of Mr. Acimovic. And the next one is Gordan --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I could ask just one very short break because the witness came to The Hague last night and we had no opportunity to show him the courtroom and -- it would take just five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection from me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection or no objection, I said. No objection, all right. Okay. There is a logistical problem in the sense that I am informed the witness is not yet here. He is on his way. Because he was somehow informed that he would start his testimony at what time? At 5.00. That means he should be here at 4.30, he should be here at 4.30. So as soon as he's here, please liaise with Mr. Zivanovic so that this logistic business is dealt with. We will be downstairs in our respective Chambers. You'll let us know and we'll come up and resume the sitting. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you need a longer break, you can have a longer break, but then we won't have a break afterwards. We'll continue until we finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We cannot do that? No? I do not dare resist. So, okay, we will be in our rooms. Please let us know and we'll come up and continue. --- Break taken at 4.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Bjelanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. We are going to start with your evidence soon. You are a witness called by the Defence of Colonel Vujadin Popovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Vinko Pandurevic"]. Before you start giving evidence, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration, which Madam Usher is showing you at the moment and handing to you. Please read it out aloud and that will be your undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, the translation was wrong on the page 30, line 17, it is said that he is witness of Colonel Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, but I said definitely Popovic. Thank you for the correction. Unless General Pandurevic wants to adopt him. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bjelanovic.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record could you please state your name and your family name?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Gordan Bjelanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of August 1966 in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us something about your educational background.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm an auto mechanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you work before the beginning of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The Party of Serbian Unity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When was that? During what period of time?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: From 1994 to 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of a paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: In April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What unit were you mobilised into?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Into the MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay with the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Until September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened then? Were you transferred to some other duty or to another unit?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was wounded in an ambush and transferred to another unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: This happened in Metali near Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you wounded? In which part of the body?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the left lower leg and in the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Having recovered from your wounds, did you go back to the MUP or were you transferred to another unit?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was transferred to another unit, to the assault detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay with that unit?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed with that unit it was re-established and became the military police battalion of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what duties did you have in that assault detachment to which you were assigned after the wounding?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was the APC driver, which was used to pull out the wounded and also to supply the VRS members with supplies, with food and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were attached to the military police of the Drina Corps, what did you do there as a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a military policeman which means I provided security for various facilities. I was also a driver for a number of high-ranking officers, and I did all the other things that were within the purview of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, can you give us a list of those tasks of the military police? What were those tasks that you performed in addition to being a driver?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I provided security for high-ranking officers who would come to the Drina Corps command. Moreover, I would bring in VRS soldiers who had deserted from the front lines, who had committed certain crimes such as theft and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about your uniforms? Did your uniforms in the Drina Corps differ from the uniforms of other members of the VRS? And if they did, could you please describe the differences?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The uniforms were the same, but we had different insignia on the left shoulder. We had an emblem with the inscription the 5th Battalion of the military police, and underneath it says the military police of Drina Corps, and there was a coat of arms and beneath that, every soldier had its own number assigned to him, from 1 upwards. As for the rest, everything was the same, the uniforms were the same. The military policemen who only controlled check-points for traffic, who provided traffic control, they had white belts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that the markings on the shoulder that you have just described were worn by all members of the police, irrespective of their affiliation?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: All save for those who worked at the command building. They did not have the same markings. For example, the cooks, the auxiliary staff, the personnel who worked in the building and who did not move around, like we policemen did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the policemen who regulated traffic at check-points wore white belts. Did military policemen wear white belts in other -- any other circumstances?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No, only when manning check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in the battalion, first of all, can you remember how many people there were, how many soldiers of the -- and military police battalion in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Those of us who came from the assault detachment, together with those who had been at the MP battalion before, there were around 100 of us in total. Maybe more. However, after some seven to 10 days later, those who didn't like being transferred to the military police asked to be sent back to their respective units which were closer to their homes, such as Milici, Sekovici, Bratunac, and so it happened. Therefore, only around 60 of us remained at the MP Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. I just wondered if we could get a date. It wasn't completely clear to me when he came from the assault group to the Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough. I was thinking of the same thing. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic and Witness, Mr. Bjelanovic, if you could see to that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I try to clarify it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelanovic, approximately or perhaps precisely, can you tell us when the assault detachment was made part of the military police of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I think in 1993. I don't recall the exact date. I think it was around August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that only around 60 of you remained in the MP Battalion, at what time was it? When was that, when there were 60 of you?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993. That's how many remained. From the moment people were being transferred to the military police, people kept leaving as well, in small groups, three or five of them, and then they would be sent to other units which were closer to their homes. And besides, we did not have the conditions necessary to billet so many policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me approximately how many MP members were there in the summer of 1995? We are particularly interested in July, if you know.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Around 40, 40 military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived, who commanded your unit of the military police, when you arrived in 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the military police was Lieutenant Miladin Matic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Who commanded that unit in 1995?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Ratko Vujovic, Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will move on to the relevant period, this being the summer of 1995, in particular July. Can you tell me approximately, and if you recall, what tasks did the military police unit have in addition to the regular military police tasks?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The military police at that time was at the front lines. We had to cover the part of the lines at Kocar where the Bratunac Brigade soldiers had left, had abandoned the front line. We had to cover it, to link up the separated parts of the front line. Some policemen remained in Vlasenica to secure buildings and man the check-point there and regulate the traffic, but it was seven or eight of them in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me precisely what your post was per establishment in July 1995? What was the name of the position and the tasks you executed?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Driver/escort. I acted as driver when needed and escorted the officers of the Drina Corps, and the building -- securing the building as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How many of you worked on the same job, had the same tasks you did?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was alone. There was another soldier later on who acted only as escort, not as driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "at that time," please tell me when precisely. Perhaps we were not on the same page.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: 1995. 1995. It was then that I was driver and an escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were driver to certain Drina Corps officers. Could you please name some of them?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: General Krstic, then the then Colonel Andric, as well as other officers as needed. I would take them wherever necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else act as driver besides you?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was the only driver of General Krstic, and Dalibor Krstic also acted as his driver. It was the two of us who acted as his drivers. Then there was Tosic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, in 1995, who was deputy commander for security in the Drina Corps? Who was the chief of the security sector?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Deputy organ for security?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The organ of security, who was also deputy commander for security.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I know it was Vujadin Popovic, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995 -- let me ask you this first: Do you remember whether the Drina Corps had any part in the operation concerning Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the dates?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall any particular dates. I can only recall the exact year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall the month?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I do. I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What month was it?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, in July 1995, did you see Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before I move on to another question in relation to that, I wanted to ask you the following. Whilst you were a member of the 5th MP Battalion, who issued you orders?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: We were issued orders by Ratko Vujovic, commander of the military police. Ratko Vujovic in turn probably received his orders from the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were with the Drina Corps military police, did you receive any orders directly from Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: To go back to where I left off, can you please recall July 1995? Did you, and where, see Vujadin Popovic? If you did, can you tell us in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him mostly in Vlasenica, because our MP Battalion building was next to the corps command building. That's where I would usually see him. I don't know what you mean exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Do you remember you, at all, any particular events, particular occasion on which you saw him, which would be out of the ordinary?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know who commanded the Drina Corps in July?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The Drina Corps command was General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he command the corps the whole month?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: He commanded the corps during the Srebrenica operation. Later, General Krstic was appointed the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, or how did you come to know, that General Krstic was appointed the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Once Srebrenica fell, in front of the Drina Corps building, the officers were lined up, the officers of the Drina Corps command, and there was a handover of duties between Generals Zivanovic and Krstic. I think at the time Krstic was still colonel. The duties were handed over and there was a lineup of the officers. General Mladic attended as well, and he directed the handover between the generals.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will not inquire about the date since you said you cannot remember precise dates, but can you tell me what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps around noon or just after noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the officers were lined up, the officers of the corps. Was the military police unit lined up as well, your unit, that is?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: We were not because many military policemen were absent. They were at the Kocari front line. There were only a few military policemen there and the personnel in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, when it was taking place, were you tasked with anything particular in Vlasenica, you and the soldiers who were there?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: We were supposed to secure the building where it was all taking place. There were also two military policemen at the check-point just outside Vlasenica controlling the traffic. There were not enough of us to provide any extended security in the town itself. There was also no need for such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean there was no need to provide any security in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did any of the officers participate in the organisation of security and the activities pertaining to the event?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In my view, Vujadin Popovic should have been in charge of security, since he was in charge of security at the command. He was in charge of building security under the circumstances that prevailed at the time, and here I mean the number of military policemen he had at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please clarify. Did you see something of the sort or is this your assumption?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw it. I saw my commander, Ratko Vujovic and Vujadin Popovic. He was on the spot. They participated in the organisation of the seminar -- ceremony. That is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Another thing: When such security is being provided, when a visit of a senior officer is expected, such as the visit of General Mladic, how much time before his arrival are things being put in place? And how long does it all last?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: When General Ratko Mladic used to come, things were being organised much earlier. We would secure the building, the route, with the critical points where enemy groups may access the route. It was all done in advance because usually we never knew the exact time of his arrival, for his security. It was for his personal safety. Nobody knew the exact time. Perhaps he would show up two or three times [as interpreted] in advance or later, and the same procedure applied once he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In translation, it is page 41, line 2. It is said two or three times. It was hours, two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: To be on the safe side, let's clear this up. Perhaps my intervention wasn't clear enough. My question was: Before the arrival of a high-ranking officer such as Mr. Mladic, how much ahead of that time did the military police have to put in place these security measures?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: At least two hours in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, if you remember, if the same applied to that particular occasion when General Mladic came to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how long it takes to put these security measures in place before such an individual's arrival?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: It depends on how long it takes for the individual to arrive. At any rate, the preparations would take as long as it would take for the general to arrive to that particular spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have an error in the interpretation. You understood my question because it says how long it takes before the arrival, whereas you were speaking about how long it took for these security measures to be implemented as of his arrival onwards; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, are these measures in place for as long as he's there and until he leaves? For instance in that case, in Vlasenica, were they in force until he left elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how did you address Mr. Popovic, by which title?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir. Or Lieutenant Colonel. Whatever the rank he held at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear other soldiers addressing him or, rather, did you hear what the form of address used by others was? I didn't understand your answer. Does it mean that that was the way everyone addressed him or you addressed him?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: All the soldiers addressed him by, "Colonel, sir," as was the case with any officer, depending on the rank the individual held.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a rule?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that rule complied with in general in the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did there ever happen that any of the soldiers would address Mr. Popovic by name or by his nickname? And did you ever witness any such situation, that such a soldier would address Mr. Popovic directly in this way?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: None of the soldiers did. Only his colleagues who were themselves officers would address him by Pop and such like. Common soldiers did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if Vujadin Popovic ever used a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: He had a car of the Golf make. We referred it to Dvojka or Golf 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Drina Corps have several vehicles, the Drina Corps have several vehicles of that same make?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you per chance remember the colour of the vehicle that he drove?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I'm going to start objecting to leading. The question could have been how many Golfs were there in the Drina Corps motor pool.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, he is right. Please adjust your --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I will adjust my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's basically too late now. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall the colour of the car he used at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if the vehicle he used was set aside for his purposes, that's to say for the purposes of the security organs, or was the vehicle used by others too?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The vehicle belonged to the security organ. What needs to be said is that the vehicle was not driven by Vujadin Popovic. It was driven by drivers. I didn't see Popovic often by the car. I saw Dusan Vucetic, who was a driver. He was the driver of the security organ while driving other vehicles too. That was his profession. That was his post. He was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that this individual drove other cars as well, does that mean that he drove other individuals, other officers, or did he only drive Popovic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: He drove others too, in the same car. There weren't enough vehicles to go around, so the same vehicle had to be used to transport other individuals as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Following this event, that's to say when you were in Vlasenica and when General Mladic arrived, did you stay on in Vlasenica or did you go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the IKM, in the direction of Zepa. IKM, that's to say the forward command post in the direction of Zepa. That's where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this on that same day or --

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
