utterances.text: No, it was on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly did you travel on your way to Zepa? What was the route you took?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the name of the place, whether Kusace or Krivace, I'm not sure. It's been a while. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what the location was and why you went there?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: There was the IKM there, where presumably Zepa was supposed to have been done. That was my understanding of it, since I saw the communications vehicles there and other vehicles present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, as you went there, do you recall what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know exactly. I believe it was around noon. We stayed there until the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing some officers there? Who did you see at the location where you got to and where you stayed until the evening hours, as you say?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw certain officers, communications officers, as well as Vujadin Popovic. I can't recall the names of all the officers who were there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there? Did you spend the night there, or did you go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed there until the evening hours, because that was when General Krstic was brought there, and we then returned to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it dark already at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else. At the time of the operation around Srebrenica, did your unit, that's to say the military police of the Drina Corps, go into the AOR of the Zvornik Brigade, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So that's your testimony, that it didn't go?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have information to the effect that certain -- in certain places around Zvornik, some soldiers were sighted with the insignias reading the military police of the Drina Corps on their arms. Since you say that the Drina Corps police -- military police did not go over there, how would you account for the fact that some individuals were spotted wearing the insignia that were normally worn only by members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Maybe I should have waited for the end of the question but the witness has given his answer and I think he's now saying -- I understood --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Asking him how he can account for other witnesses is not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic? He may have an explanation. So I think it's a very valid question. Go ahead, Mr. Bjelanovic. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Then go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since there were around a hundred of us, soldiers of the Drina Corps, members of the military police, who wore insignia on our left arms, the soldiers would normally retain the insignia on their uniform, so even if they ceased being members of the military police and became members of other units of the Drina Corps, they kept the insignia. I myself saw them wearing the insignia. It facilitated their movement because they didn't have personal vehicles at their disposal, it would be much easier for them to find transportation from one place to another. So they abused the insignia. I know that Ratko Vujovic requested that the insignia be given back to the military police. We ourselves went back to give the insignia back to the unit, but very few people did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all. Thank you, Mr. Bjelanovic. I don't have further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Ostojic? You had asked for 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Nikolic, you confirm that you have no questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Madam. Mr. Lazarevic? You had asked for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau, you had asked for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci, Madam. Mr. Josse, you had asked for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Same as my learned friends, no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Sarapa, you had indicated no cross-examination. Do you stick to that or have you thought about changing your mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Nicholls, you had asked for two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know we had a break recently. If I could have a short break to meet with Mr. McCloskey, I may be able to make this much shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I dread to ask you, Madam Registrar, in case you tell me no, we can't. It's half past 5.00. If we have the break now, would it be okay? Yes? Okay. Thank you. So we'll have 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelanovic, my name as the Judges told you is Julian Nicholls. I'll be asking you some questions now, okay?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When did you first meet Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Vujadin Popovic? When I joined the 5th Battalion of the military police in the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Before that you had never met him in any capacity at all?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. When you were in that -- I'll get the name right -- assault detachment, who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander was Miso Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember the name Miroslav Kraljevic, Milos Lakic, were they in that detachment with you?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Mica Kraljevic replaced Miso Pelemis as the commander of the assault detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 339 up, please? Your Honour, just for the transcript I believe the witness said Miso Pelemis and -- there we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at the person at number 43, I'm sorry, I don't have a translation of this, Your Honour, but it's a list, it's simply a list, and the heading states, "List of members of the VP 7118 Han Pijesak assault detachment," in parentheses. This is your assault detachment, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You recognise some of these names on here, I guess, if you take a moment?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the second page quickly. And we've got there, Commandant Major Vujadin Popovic and his signature. Right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Vujadin Popovic was not the commander of the assault detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you have an explanation, then, for this document, which lists your members and him signing off on the list of members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May I see the original of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't have it in court with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have strong doubt in the authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a speaking objection which is not necessary. I don't have the original with me in court but I can provide it to him at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I think that's how it's done. I think at this moment making such a statement in the presence of the witness is not exactly what you should be doing. Please proceed, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can I -- may I answer the question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just asking if he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation of why Mr. Popovic has signed this document?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who could have signed this. I'm not familiar with Mr. Vujadin Popovic's signature. I never saw any documents with signatures. I was a mere member of the detachment that just carried out orders. I never had an occasion to look at any documents. As for the names, I am familiar with the names of these people, some of whom were indeed members of the assault detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let's now change topics and talk about what you were doing, you personally, during the month of July 1995. All right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, just take me through very briefly that month, let's start off, first week of July, what are your duties as a driver and escort? What are you doing?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I was in Vlasenica at the time, in the Military Police Battalion, for a short while I was General Krstic's driver. I provided the security for the building, and I did everything else that a military policeman is supposed to do when on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was the short time when you were his driver, from when to when, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but, for example, I would take him somewhere in the morning and I would return on the same day. I was not his regular driver. He had his own driver that took him around, and I would join as a driver and as an escort to also provide security for General Krstic. That was my main role.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Who was his regular driver, again? Dalibor Krstic, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know that man, Dalibor Krstic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said you would take Krstic somewhere in the morning and return the same day. Where are some of the places that you would take him? And I want to start off with before the fall of Srebrenica. Where did you take General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Before the fall of Srebrenica, I took General Krstic to an area between Bratunac and Potocari, where the separation line was. Then he would pay a visit to the brigade, he would meet up with some people from the brigade, and I would take him back to Vlasenica the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long is this before the fall of Srebrenica? How many days?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand, what do you mean by how many days?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How many days? You said before the fall of Srebrenica you took General Krstic to Bratunac and Potocari and the separation line. I'm asking you how many days before the fall was this. If you don't remember, you don't remember, but that's the question, though.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know exactly but I know that this was before Srebrenica, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember the fall of Srebrenica? Or liberation?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know when it happened. I remember when it happened. But I was not in Srebrenica or anywhere near so as to know what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. When did it fall, if you remember? What's the date?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I think on the 12th or the 13th of July thereabouts. I don't know exactly. I don't know which of the two dates but I know that it was on one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Whatever the date it was, where were you when Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in a place called Vuksic Polje. That's where my wife hails from. And my brother-in-law, my wife's brother, was supposed to be sent off to the VRS army. This is according to our Serbian customs, whenever somebody is supposed to join the army, he is given a big sendoff. However, this time, the send-off was very short, maybe only two or three hours. And then we heard that Muslim soldiers killed a man and wounded another in that same village, in front of Milici, some six kilometres in front of Milici. That's what interrupted our celebration. We did not go on partying. We had to take care of the women and children who were there. And I remained in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So essentially the day Srebrenica falls, you had the day off for this traditional celebration? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's one day. Actually it was in the evening, just one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And then tell me about the next day. Did you stay in that village, Vuksic Polje, to protect the women and children, or what did you do?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I returned to Vlasenica, to the police, and the other people stayed there. It's different when it's daylight. People came from Milici, members of that brigade came, and obviously they protected not only that village but also all the other villages through which armed members of the Muslim army were passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So then the next day, what time do you get back to Vlasenica, to the Drina Corps headquarters, the day after Srebrenica falls?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I can't remember the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, before lunch, after lunch?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: When Srebrenica fell, maybe you did not understand me. It was not before lunch. It was much after lunch. It all happened in the evening hours, not during the day. It was rather later in the evening and on the following day I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's be clear. You talked about the day Srebrenica fell which was -- you've explained that. I'm talking about the next day when you said you got back to Vlasenica. I want to know what time you returned to Vlasenica on the day after Srebrenica fell, please. My question was, if you recall if it was before or after lunch, if you can give me some ballpark time?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. I can't remember. I can't remember exactly when that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And what were your duties for that day, after Srebrenica fell? What was your job?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember what I did. I did my job. I was a member of the military police. And basically that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You stayed at Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, think carefully. What did you do that day? If you don't remember, don't guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The witness already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Having had time to think carefully, do you have an answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I answered that I was in Vlasenica after the fall of Srebrenica, and there was a handover between General Krstic and General Zivanovic. I remember that I was there. I did not leave Vlasenica after the fall of Srebrenica, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But when it comes to the exact dates and times, it's difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when he said, "I think so," that's what he meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So I think I understand now. At the fall, you had a little bit of time off during the fall of Srebrenica to attend this relative's celebration, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in a nutshell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The following day at some time, you don't remember when exactly, you returned to Vlasenica, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The next event you remember is this ceremony where General Krstic was formally announced by Mladic to be commander of the Drina Corps, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and the day following that, according to your testimony, after that ceremony, you go to Krivace to the Zepa IKM, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And you drive General Krstic to the Krivace IKM, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you get to that IKM, you remember apparently clearly seeing Vujadin Popovic there. Who else did you see there?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw some officers from the 2nd Romanija Brigade. I also saw the communications officers, but I just saw them briefly because I stayed with the vehicle most of the time. We did not follow General Krstic to see who he would be talking to. I could only talk to my peers, other foot soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember the names of any of these officers, communications officers, 2nd Romanija Brigade personnel that you saw at the IKM on that day?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that Colonel Miljanovic was there because I remember him. I don't know who the communications officers were. There were two. But I don't know whether they were Drljaca or Jevcic. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when was the first time that you explained all of this, your recollection of this ceremony in Vlasenica and going to Zepa, when was the first time you explained that to Popovic's Defence counsel? When did they get in contact with you?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Last year they got in contact with me. So the answer would be last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And they asked you questions about these events and when and where you'd seen Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did they help you remember, refresh your recollection with any other statements or transcripts or documents, since you can't remember the dates?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Whatever they asked me about Vujadin Popovic, they would not suggest to me where I might have seen him. They just asked me where I saw him and I would tell them, and they would make a record of that, and they didn't ask me anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Which means whatever I could remember, I would tell them and amongst other things where I saw Vujadin Popovic, if I could remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. And it wasn't that easy for you to remember, was it? I can see from the difficulty you're having today with some of these dates and times.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't remember the dates. I can remember the year or approximately the month, but the exact dates. I was wounded on two occasions, and I can't even remember the exact dates when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Even if you asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And this is the first time since these events during the war that you had to sit down with a lawyer and try to remember everything and go through it and explain it?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And did you -- did you sign any kind of written statement or anything like that when you met with Mr. Popovic's lawyers?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try to help you remember some things. Do you remember being contacted -- let me finish the question -- do you remember being contacted by the Defence team for General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you tell the witness approximately when?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell him exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The 9th of March 2001, in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And that is where you met with attorneys for General Krstic, to talk about what you remembered, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So when I said to you just a moment ago, on page 57, at line 13 that this was the first time when you met with Mr. Popovic's lawyers to go through these events and try to remember these things and go through them, that wasn't true, was it? Did you make a mistake?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not understand your question. Could you now explain what you mean, what I'm supposed to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I asked you a moment ago whether, when you met with Mr. Popovic's lawyers and went down and had to go through the events of the war and try to remember these times around the period we are talking about today, if that was the first time you sat down with a lawyer and you said it was. And now I'm asking if you made a mistake, if you couldn't remember then and you remember now, you were being untruthful? How come you said that a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not understand what you were asking, but I remember it well, when I provided a statement to Defence counsel Petrusic at the then command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica concerning General Krstic, but I did not understand this question of yours this time around. This was the first time at that time when I met with any Defence team representing General Krstic, and the second time representing Vujadin Popovic, and the first statement that I provided to the Defence team of General Krstic, I signed -- I signed that, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that was in 2001, so much closer to the events we are talking about, July 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you were being contacted as a potential witness for the Defence, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Most probably, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You didn't know? Is it probably or you knew? I want you to be as precise as you can. Didn't they tell you they think you might be a Defence witness when they took a statement from you?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that they must have wanted that from me. I don't know. I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you knew that it was important, when you were making a statement, as a potential Defence witness, to tell the truth, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You signed this statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you knew that this statement and what you said in it could be the basis for your evidence in the trial for your former commander, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take a look at the statement. That's 3398. Let's go to the last page. I hope this is all there in the B/C/S. "The record of the conversation was read aloud to the witness. By affixing his signature at the bottom of the records, the witness confirmed that he had no objections, Vlasenica, 9 March 2001." That's what it says, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could we turn the page? We can make it bigger. That is your signature, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to go to page 2 of the document, should be 2 in both languages. Okay? Now, if we can scroll down a bit for the witness. Up a bit, please. Okay. We've got a question here: Were you General Krstic's driver and escort in Srebrenica in the period 5th July 1995 onwards? And you answered: In the period from 5 July 1995 onwards, Dalibor Krstic, Vlado Tosic and I were General Krstic's drivers and escorts. I was in Srebrenica in that period from 5 to 12 July until we left Srebrenica. It is certain that Dalibor Krstic, Vlado Tosic and I were present as drivers and escorts that whole time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, stop there for the time being. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that part of this sentence is not properly translated, because the witness said in B/C/S. [Interpretation] "Therefore I was at Srebrenica," not "in Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go on. Otherwise we have a break to study the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Be this as it may -- so now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed but thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So now, seven years ago, when you were called to be a potential Defence witness for General Krstic, knowing that you might be a witness, you stated that you were in or at Srebrenica the entire time from 5 to 12 July, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Not between the 5th and the 12th. I wasn't there through all those days. For example, I would be there a day and then I would leave and then go back. It was Krstic, Tosic and I, but we as the drivers were not in Srebrenica all together. Between the 5th and the 12th, I may have been there for a day or two. The rest, it was Krstic or Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: There were three drivers, and we took turns and rested, and if all three of us worked at the same time, there would be no time for rest for any of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It still doesn't provide an explanation, Mr. Nicholls and Witness, because his statement explains also that Tosic was wounded after Srebrenica and therefore Krstic and he stayed on as drivers and escorts, except that Krstic was absent, Dalibor Krstic, was absent for probably two or three days. If he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Vlasenica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm speaking -- I recollect with respect to the wounding of Tosic but I'm certain Krstic was the driver at the time of Srebrenica and that he did not leave that area. It seems pretty confusing. If he could explain exactly what happened or what he meant to say in that statement in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But if you could explain, Witness, but first what I want you to explain is why you said in that statement it's very clear I was at, it may say in the B/C/S, or in Srebrenica in that period from 5 to 12 July until we left Srebrenica. Why did you say that if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't in Srebrenica as a driver. When I spoke about General Krstic, I meant the three drivers as a whole. I didn't have myself in mind alone. I was trying to deal with the whole situation. When I was driving Mr. Krstic, I never took him into Srebrenica but to Pribicevac, which is above Srebrenica, Potocari, and the surrounding locations of Srebrenica. Dalibor Krstic drove General Krstic into Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's clear enough now, unless you want to pursue it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, and just to be clear from the portion you were reading, the part where Dalibor Krstic was absent was during the Zepa operation, that's what you said, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Dalibor Krstic was not absent due to the Zepa operation. When I drove General Krstic there, I would be there for a day. I wasn't his permanent driver. I was a reserve driver so to say. I was both driver and escort, if I was in the vehicle, I wasn't necessarily driving all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at the very first paragraph for a minute. Page 1. Okay, just to be clear, there, under where it says statement, izjavu, you say I was -- I know General Radislav Krstic. I was his driver and escort. I started my job in approximately mid-1995 and you say that you worked with Dalibor Krstic as well. You didn't put anywhere there in this statement as a potential Defence witness that you were a reserve driver and not the main driver, did you?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't. That is correct. Per establishment, I was driver and escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, let's go to page 2. Scroll down, please. Question: Were you on Potocari and 12 July 1995? That is the day after Srebrenica fell. Answer: I remember that we were in Potocari and we stayed there briefly. Around 20 minutes, and then we went via Pribicevac to Vigor [phoen]. We did not pass through Srebrenica on that day or on that occasion. So now when you were getting ready to testify possibly for General Krstic in his Defence, you are in Potocari. When you're here testifying for Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, you state that were you in Vlasenica the entire time after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me explain. I remember that we were in Potocari but not in Potocari itself. This was just before Potocari. I didn't know the exact name of that location but now I know that it's called Zuti Most or the Yellow Bridge. Another thing, Pribicevac, even had we been in Srebrenica we would not have been able to reach Pribicevac from Srebrenica but from Bratunac. That would indicate that we were not in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You haven't answered the question. The question is could you -- can you explain if what you've just said is true that you were on a part of the road near Potocari at Zuti Most, how can you reconcile that with your previous statement that you had not moved from Vlasenica after the fall of Srebrenica. This is the question, which you haven't answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember whether it was the 12th or the 13th or the 13th in the evening or the 12th in the evening when I was in Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, when you were going to testify -- when you gave to statement to the Defence for General Krstic, go through this whole thing, you were assisting what he wanted to say, which is that he was gone by the 12th of July. As part of that alibi, so to speak, you put yourself with him on the 12th of July in Potocari, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Just before Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right. Now, here you have testified under oath the entire time after the fall of Srebrenica, you were in Vlasenica, you were there from the fall until the handover ceremony. Now, you either have a terrible memory and can't remember being in Potocari after the fall of Srebrenica today or you have lied in one of these statements. I'm asking you to explain that.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: When Srebrenica fell, of course it didn't fall in a day. At that time, I was not in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you or were you not in Vlasenica, as you testified under oath earlier today, from the fall of Srebrenica until the morning when you went to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll read it to you. Were you, you, or were you not, in Vlasenica, meaning Drina Corps command, as you testified under oath earlier today, meaning here a little while ago, from the fall of Srebrenica until the morning after the handover ceremony when you went to Zepa? I'm asking you that question again, yes or no, were you there the whole time?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Vlasenica, when the handover took place and when I left for Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You're not answering the question. And I think you're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we've heard enough on that. Go to your next question. Mr. Bjelanovic, do you want to answer the question? It's being put to you that you are making two conflicting statements, one today and one seven years ago. Which one is the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one I stated today is the truth. As for the rest, I don't remember and it's not clear to me. I don't understand. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But when you made the statement to Mr. Petrusic, did you lie to him, when you said that you were near Potocari on the 12th of July? And if you did, why -- what interest did you have to lie to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not lie. When I used to come there with General Krstic, because... I used to go to Vlasenica but not only in his car and not only General Krstic, and I know that I was bringing some pills, not with his car. We used to come with another car. So it's not like that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Nicholls, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you talked about this handover ceremony. You talked about this handover ceremony and that the next day you went to Krivace IKM. The night of the handover ceremony, Popovic, Vujadin Popovic, stayed at the Hotel Fontana in Bratunac, correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You didn't know where he was that night?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You don't know where he was that morning, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we have any foundation for this statement that Mr. Popovic was in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I'll do it now. 457, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that to come up, you already said on direct that the driver for Popovic was Dusan Vucetic, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have page 13 of the B/C/S and page 7 of the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, we have the original here because I can't tell in the B/C/S how much is cut off but in the English, it's very clear. This is a bill from the 15th of July -- my friend is standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a bill but not date of his staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the second time today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are rules that need to be followed. If you look at the top of the page, you have a date there, and what Mr. Nicholls said was very clear. He said this is a bill from the 15th of July. So please, you will have a right to re-examine the witness later on but not to interrupt in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I asked the foundation for his statement that Mr. Popovic spent the night on 13th -- or this night in Bratunac. The specific night. What night? It is the bill. It is a bill, not anything about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No arguments and submissions in the presence of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could put the original on the ELMO, we could see the entire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think it will close -- bring the discussion to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, this is a -- what you're seeing, Witness, and if you want, you can look to the right, is an original receipt from the Hotel Fontana. 15 July 1995 is the date of this bill, and it states that it's to the command of the Bratunac Brigade, Bratunac paying or at the top, and it says accommodation in Hotel Fontana for Colonel Vujadin Popovic, amount two at 35 dinars for a total of 70 dinars. Now, doesn't this indicate to you that he paid a bill for two nights on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a misstatement again. There is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why is it a misstatement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There isn't anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why is it a misstatement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to -- if -- he didn't pay anything. It is a bill sent to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From that -- he's considering it an invoice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And not a receipt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's now just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not waste time on it because basically what you're after is the date and nothing else, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And now very quickly on this document, one more, English page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness hasn't answered the question, and I don't know whether he is in a position to answer the question, having said that he didn't know whether he had stayed or where he was. Could you go back to your original question, Mr. Nicholls, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Kwon is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, see if this helps you remember. Looking at this bill from the Hotel Fontana for the 15th of July 1995, the date on the bill for an amount of two at 35 dinars for a total of 70 dinars, doesn't this indicate to you that there was a bill for two nights' stay of Vujadin Popovic, the bill was made out on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I am concerned, these invoices could be presented by whoever wanted to do so. As for this one, I can't tell you anything. When we were there, anyone could come in with invoices. To me, this one doesn't say anything. If General Krstic, say, spent the night at the Fontana, he certainly wouldn't be the person paying for it. It could be signed by anyone, and, well, in any case, I think he could spend the night at that hotel for free, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When did you stay at the hotel --

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see Vujadin Popovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. When -- when -- when did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could quickly look at page 5 of the English, page 9 of the B/C/S, very simple question, sir, this is a bill for the 15th of July 1995 for driver as well as Colonel Krsmanvic for driver Djule Vucetic. That's Popovic's driver, isn't it? Also got a bill on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And very quickly, if we can look at page 11 of the English, page 21 of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the previous question, we read the following: [In English] Vucetic, Popovic's driver, also got a bill on the 15th. [Interpretation] I don't think that any of these documents was addressed to any of these people. These documents are addressed to the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Do you wish to comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think it's significant, Your Honour. It's a bill for the person who was staying at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But technically she is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: She is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was being invoiced is the Bratunac Brigade command. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to indicate that the witness already answered that Mr. Vucetic was not just the driver of Popovic. It's in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is the third time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, this is highly irregular. What is being suggested to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: His question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry, stop. The question that was put to the witness is does it result to you from this document that this Vucetic, who was incidentally Popovic's driver, whether it was full time or not is another matter, stayed at the hotel on -- or an invoice was issued for his stay in the hotel on the 15th of July? So let's please keep everything in the proper perspective because otherwise I will have to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now if we look at the one we have up on the screen, Witness.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I didn't ask my question. Do you have something to say?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: I do. May I comment these last two invoices? I saw that they were incorrect. I disagree with them. On this invoice, it says Dalibor Krstic spent eight nights, eight times 35, at the Fontana Hotel. That is not correct. I know it for sure. I spent time with Dalibor Krstic even after Srebrenica had fallen. He told me that he wasn't staying at the hotel at that time but with his parents. They could have written that Vujadin Popovic was at the hotel, although he may not have been. They could have written anything. Say Djule Vucetic, if he was there it doesn't necessarily mean that he drove Mr. Popovic there. He could have come with Krsmanvic or with anyone else. As for the rest of the invoices, they were in Popovic's name, but we see from this one that Dalibor did not spend the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And his parents live in Bratunac very close to the hotel, don't they? That's where he spent the night, right?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Not so close. Dalibor Krstic was with his parents, yes, so he wasn't at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in Bratunac, in Bratunac, during this period?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Bratunac, well, the outskirts, Dalibor Krstic, but he's still on this invoice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And he was there as the driver and escort for General Krstic, correct, when he was in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And Tosic was General Krstic's escort at that time?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And according to you, you were not, although you said you were in your statement, and I put it to you that -- we have one minute left -- you said that in your statement, you knew it wasn't true, because you were trying to help General Krstic in his defence that he was gone by the 12th.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: He was gone before the 12th where? Where to? I don't understand. I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That he was gone from the Srebrenica Drina Corps command area before the 13th.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN BJELANOVIC
utterances.text: The Drina Corps command, well, you have to clarify it for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we'll leave that for tomorrow. How much longer do you have so that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll think about it, Your Honour, and cut it shorter, just a couple more topics, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I will notify my friends and the Court since we are in the afternoon if I'm able to make it extremely shorter or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And please have the next witness ready for tomorrow. And the one which we have scheduled for Friday ready just in case. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have just two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, the one on Monday is --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know, I know, so we can't get him here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I bring both of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You have understood me actually. Please do your best to see how we go about this. Thanks. Have a nice evening and we'll reconvene tomorrow in the afternoon, then. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
